items.note: Page (19 Nov 2019) title matches. 2.90 -> 4.00 EUR/h (page also mentions 4.40 with mobile ticket, not claimed), Mon-Sat 9-22, 5 EUR overnight flat rate, last change Dec 2015, council vote 'planned for' 6 Feb 2020, no outcome reported. Kept as a proposal.

Page (2 May 2024) refers to a resolution of June 2020 under which 25 further zones were to be added to the existing 31 resident-parking zones. The figure 56 is not stated (only implied by 31+25). Page does not state that Mobility Plan D was 'adopted in 2019' as such; it only cites the 2019 plan's goals of redistributing street space and reorganising public parking. The page also says this extension was later folded into a newer resolution (Bilk and Flingern pilot areas), so 'extended' overstates completion.
items.corrected_text: A resolution passed in June 2020 provided for 25 further resident-parking zones on top of the existing 31; a later resolution folded this extension in and picked Bilk and Flingern as pilot areas. The page ties the parking policy to the goals of the 2019 Mobility Plan D.

items.note: Page dated 21 Sep 2020; title matches. 660 spaces on five levels, barcode + number-plate recognition, dynamic pricing by capacity utilisation, personal RFID chip opening barriers contactlessly, 24 E.ON charging points all stated; APCOA Parking Deutschland 'has taken over the operation'.

Page dated 13 Jan 2021; title matches. Q-Park takes over Liesegangstrasse garage (formerly Galeria Kaufhof Karstadt), name 'Stadtmitte', 519 spaces on six levels, online reservation and number-plate recognition being prepared, short-stay tariff 2.50 EUR/h, no EV charging offered, Q-Park runs 12 facilities in Duesseldorf.

Page dated 14 Jun 2021, title matches. Settlement of the lawsuit against the Duesseldorf air quality plan, no (area-wide) driving bans, environment-sensitive signal control, new U81 line linking main station, fairgrounds and airport, expansion of EV charging infrastructure, and designation of P+R parking are all stated. But Tempo 30 is named only for Merowingerstrasse, not 'key streets'; 'more park-and-ride' is 'Ausweisung von P+R-Parkplaetzen' (designation of P+R spaces).
items.corrected_text: The State of North Rhine-Westphalia, the City of Duesseldorf and Deutsche Umwelthilfe settled the air-quality lawsuit out of court; the state said there would be no driving bans. The package includes environment-sensitive signal control, Tempo 30 on Merowingerstrasse, designation of park-and-ride parking, expansion of EV charging infrastructure and a new U81 line linking the main station, fairgrounds and airport.

items.note: Page dated 27 Sep 2022; title matches. Mayor Keller suspends/announces suspension of the planned increase in resident parking fee (currently 25 EUR/yr), reasoning about households burdened by rising energy costs; CDU agreed, Greens criticised. Greens are described as coalition partner in the headline ('Schwarz-Gruen').

Page dated 7 Mar 2023, title matches. The plan (25 EUR -> 360/300/240 EUR in zones 1/2/3, implementation expected by end of 2023 after passing political bodies) is stated. The second half (September 2023 taxpayers' association article, federal court ruling of 13 June 2023 in a Freiburg case, city pursuing a socially compatible fee) is NOT on this page; it comes from a different source and cannot be attributed to this URL. Page does mention a 75 percent reduction for Duesselpass holders and housing-benefit recipients.
items.corrected_text: CDU and Greens presented a plan to raise resident parking permits from 25 euros to 360 euros (zone 1), 300 euros (zone 2) and 240 euros (zone 3) per year, with implementation expected by the end of 2023 once the draft had passed the political bodies. The plan was a proposal at this point.

items.note: electrive.net, 25 Jan 2023 (updated 5 Mar 2024); title matches. More than 4,000 new charge points in garages in Germany and Austria 2023-2025, AC up to 22 kW, first Duesseldorf charge point expected in February, six garages in Duesseldorf, about 30 charge points per site on average.

Page title matches; page dated 3 May 2024 and reports the Carlsplatz redesign ceremony that day; it does not give an opening date for the charging park. Charging park with more than 60 charge points on the roof of the IDR garage is stated. The 900,000 EUR (of which NRW paid 520,000) is the cost of the whole Carlsplatz redesign (14 months), not of a garage renovation. The four XXL accessible spaces are on Benrather Strasse and Hohe Strasse (streets), not in the garage.
items.corrected_text: In a report on the completed redesign of Carlsplatz (3 May 2024), a new charging park with more than 60 charge points on the roof of the IDR garage at Carlsplatz is mentioned. The Carlsplatz redesign cost 900,000 euros and also created four XXL accessible spaces on neighbouring streets.

items.note: parking.net, 29 May 2024; title matches. Multi-storey garage at Medical Center Duesseldorf, almost 300 spaces, 130 permanent spaces sold, APCOA Duesseldorf locations now ten, ticketless entry/exit, cashless payment option. ('Underground' not independently verified in the fetch but not material; page described as multi-storey car park.)

Page dated 27 Apr 2024, title matches; draft date 2024-04 is acceptable. Both Kaufhof Koe and Schadowstrasse stores remain; Galeria HQ to move from Essen to Schadowstrasse; 16 stores on the closure list. Insolvency proceedings opening 1 April 2024 confirmed.

ecomento.de, 15 Jan 2026; title matches (page uses 'Apcoa'). 307 new charge points in garages in operation in 2025; in Duesseldorf, 9 charge points in total at Medical Center and DJC Nikko. 'across Germany' consistent with title.

corrected_summary: Since 2019 Duesseldorf has planned higher on-street parking prices and more resident-parking zones; a 2021 settlement on air quality included no driving bans and listed park-and-ride and EV-charging expansion among its measures. Operators of city-centre garages have added number-plate recognition, ticketless entry and EV charging. After the 2024 Galeria insolvency proceedings both Duesseldorf Galeria stores were to remain open.
